title: Soft Layered Wholemeal Chapati
summary: A part-wholemeal dough is rested, rolled thin, oiled, rolled into a log, sliced and pressed into spirals, then rolled out again and cooked in a hot pan with a little oil.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Stir the flours and salt, add 2 tbsp oil and the warm water and knead 6-8 minutes until smooth. Cover and rest 30 minutes.

steps.title: Roll and oil
steps.text: Roll into a thin 30 x 45 cm rectangle, brush with about 1 tbsp oil and dust lightly with flour.

steps.title: Coil
steps.text: Roll up tightly from a long side, cut into 8, stand each cut side up and press into a disc. Cover and rest 20 minutes.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Roll each disc into a 22-24 cm round, turning as you go.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Heat a dry pan over medium-high heat, brush with oil and cook each chapati about 1 minute until bubbly and spotted brown. Brush with oil, flip and cook 45-60 seconds, pressing so it puffs.

steps.title: Keep warm
steps.text: Stack in a tea towel while you cook the rest. Serve warm with dal or curry.

tips: Resting the dough twice makes it easy to roll thin without springing back.
The oil between the layers is what makes chapati flaky.
Stacking them in a towel steams them soft.
storage: Keep wrapped at room temperature and eat within 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month. Refresh in a hot oven for a few minutes. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
